source_name: Integritás Hatóság (Integrity Authority) – analyses and annual integrity report
why_relevant: EU-conditionality body with statutory powers over procurement using EU funds; it can demand re-runs and refer cases. Its 2025 annual integrity report (published 30 June 2026, ~322 pages) gives a system-wide analysis of overpricing, single-bidder competition and — critically — flags that Közbeszerzési és Ellátási Főigazgatóság central purchases worth >HUF 500bn are missing from the public procurement platform. It also publishes explainer material on remedies against KDB decisions.

source_name: Közbeszerzési Hatóság – Éves beszámolók (annual report to Parliament) and gyorsjelentés
why_relevant: Statutory annual report to Parliament covering remedy-proceeding experience and statistics: number of KDB proceedings, fines (~HUF 1.275bn), procedure counts and values (7,592 successful procedures worth HUF 3,664bn in 2024). Gives the denominator for judging how contested the banking/payments segment is.

source_name: Közbeszerzési Hatóság elnöki tájékoztatók (President's guidance notices)
why_relevant: Guidance distilling KDB and court practice (e.g. on self-cleaning / öntisztázás under Kbt. 64. and 188. §), which explains exclusion grounds that can knock a bank or acquirer out of a tender and predicts how future disputes will be decided.

source_name: Közbeszerzési kisokos – jogorvoslat (remedies explainer / actor map)
why_relevant: Authoritative map of the remedies architecture: who may file (ügyfélképesség), KDB procedure, the exclusive jurisdiction of the Fővárosi Törvényszék, and onward review. Best single artefact for building the cell's actor map and glossary.

Audit authority for EU funds; its audits explicitly cover the procurement dimension (document review and on-site checks) and drive irregularity (szabálytalansági) proceedings and financial corrections. Relevant where banking/payment services are procured inside EU-funded programmes.

source_name: KiMitTud – FOI request archive (EUTAF and other audit bodies)
why_relevant: Public archive of freedom-of-information requests and the authorities' answers. Where audit/remedy documents are not proactively published, past FOI answers are often the only public route, and the archive shows what a given body has already released.

source_name: Integrity Watch Hungary / Tenderbajnok (Transparency International Hungary)
why_relevant: Analytical database of companies winning public funds, their procurement record, ownership background and political connections. Useful to reconstruct the bidder set around contested banking/payment contracts and to spot repeat winners whose awards get challenged.

source_name: K-Monitor adatbázis (public-funds news and case archive)
why_relevant: Tagged archive of Hungarian press coverage on public money, including procurement disputes and audit findings, with entity and tag indexing. A practical shortcut to find which contested contracts got media attention and to snowball to the underlying decisions.

Investigative outlet that routinely surfaces audit and procurement documents, translated the Integrity Authority's 322-page annual report into Hungarian, and reports OLAF findings on Hungarian cases. Often the earliest accessible narrative of an audit or remedies outcome.

source_name: Jogi Fórum / Jogászvilág / Adó Online – procurement & competition legal press
why_relevant: Hungarian legal trade press that reports court outcomes in payments/competition litigation (e.g. the Fővárosi Törvényszék annulling the GVH interchange decision) and procurement-law developments, with case numbers that let you jump to the primary decision.

source_name: OLAF annual report + EPPO Hungary (EU-level fraud/audit layer)
why_relevant: OLAF annual reports and case summaries flag Hungarian procurement manipulation, conflicts of interest and artificial cost inflation; Hungary has applied to join EPPO with operations expected from early 2027 and retroactive jurisdiction back to 2021. This becomes a growing disclosure channel for contested contracts, including EU-funded IT/payments procurement.

source_name: Nemzeti Jogszabálytár (NJT) – Kbt. and institutional instructions
why_relevant: Consolidated statute database holding the Public Procurement Act (Kbt., 2015. évi CXLIII. tv.) and the internal instructions (utasítás) of ÁSZ and EUTAF that define their audit scope. Needed to interpret decision citations and to detect scope changes in the remedies regime.

source_name: NKE / academic analyses of KDB procedure and procurement litigation
why_relevant: Monograph-grade description of KDB procedure and procurement litigation, plus doctoral work on EU-funded procurement irregularities. Best for calibrating how to read decisions, deadlines, standing and the appeal chain — i.e. collection design rather than content.

source_subtype: commercial tender + grant aggregator and bid consultancy
why_relevant: Hungarian aggregator combining közbeszerzés monitoring with EU/national grant (pályázat) monitoring and bid-writing services. The dual tender+grant coverage matters for banking/payments because Hungarian financial-sector modernisation is often funded through grant programmes before it becomes a formal procurement, giving earlier lead-time signal than TED.

Expert-curated Hungarian tenderfigyelés service that attaches short specialist interpretation to each matched notice rather than raw alerting. The commentary layer is a secondary intelligence asset: it reveals how Hungarian bid practitioners read ambiguous specifications, useful when assessing whether a bank/payments notice is genuinely contestable or pre-wired.

Hungarian consultancy-run tender monitoring product. Adds vendor diversity to the HU aggregator map and, as a consultancy, its published references and case pages can indirectly reveal which Hungarian buyers and suppliers are active in IT/financial-services procurement.

Bilingual HU/EN bid-support firm whose site maintains a 'tendering interfaces' page mapping TED, EKR and the Hungarian notice systems. Best used as a pointer source: it documents the plumbing of Hungarian procurement publication and explains which interface carries which notice type, which accelerates building the A2 source graph.

Additional Hungarian tender-services provider surfaced by local-language search. Included for completeness of the HU vendor map; usefulness for banking/payments specifically is unconfirmed and its offering was not inspected in depth.

Hungarian pályázatfigyelő (grant/tender watch) service. Grant-side monitoring gives upstream signal on funded modernisation programmes that later convert into banking/payments procurement, complementing the notice-side aggregators.

source_subtype: grant aggregator with free public listings
why_relevant: Broad Hungarian grant-watch aggregator serving companies, municipalities and institutions. Its public listing of open calls is a free, low-friction way to see which Hungarian funding lines touch digitalisation and financial infrastructure before procurement notices appear.

One of the older Hungarian grant/tender portals with an established free public feed of calls. Useful as a redundancy source and for older archived calls that newer commercial platforms may not retain.

Non-commercial but functionally the strongest open aggregator for this cell: it collects, cleans and republishes contracting data for 35 jurisdictions including Hungary, drawing from BOTH TED and the national Közbeszerzési Hatóság portal - which means it captures below-EU-threshold Hungarian contracts. Run by the Government Transparency Institute (Hungary-based), it exposes buyer/supplier analytics and integrity indicators, giving structured award-notice history for HU banking/payments buyers without a paywall.

source_subtype: CEE procurement data vendor / data-quality analyst
why_relevant: Czech CEE-rooted procurement data company that processes tender data for 50+ countries and was a DIGIWHIST/Opentender consortium partner; also co-authored the Open Contracting Partnership EU data-quality report. Relevant as a CEE-wide commercial data supplier that can deliver normalised Hungarian award data, and as an authority on how reliable Hungarian publication actually is.

source_subtype: pan-European commercial tender aggregator + eTendering platform
why_relevant: Europe's largest commercial procurement platform group, consolidating national, regional and EU-level tender sources into one hub and operating buyer-side eTendering as well. Relevant to this cell as the dominant pan-European subscription aggregator a Hungarian bidder would plausibly use; its buyer-side portals also occasionally host the actual RFP for regional buyers.

EU-wide procurement intelligence platform aggregating tender notices across member states with status tracking and notifications, offering a 14-day free trial. Useful as a cheap, quickly-trialable cross-check on TED-derived Hungarian notice recall for banking/payments CPV codes.

source_subtype: commercial tender alerting service with public source documentation
why_relevant: Modern alerting service aggregating TED plus 50+ procurement portals with delivery to email or Slack. Its per-source documentation pages are themselves a pointer asset - they enumerate which national portals are indexed, useful for validating whether Hungarian sources beyond TED are genuinely covered.

source_subtype: global commercial tender database with country+sector verticals
why_relevant: Global commercial tender database maintaining a Hungary country section and, notably, an explicit banks/financial-sector vertical page - one of the very few aggregators observed that pre-segments Hungarian tenders by banking. Directly on-topic for this run's sector focus even though such global aggregators are typically thin and TED-derived.
